focus: Angle 4's security half — secret leakage paths, token storage, spoofed chat users and who may approve, tested against the runtime's record shape, the vault's storage claim and the channel link's identity model.
noveltyJustification: All three findings are new: the keychain argv exposure accepted rather than fixed, the conversation JSONL outside the literal-check list, and the linked non-approver dispatch rule left unstated.
keyQuestions: Security and failure modes: secret leakage, token storage, spoofed chat users, who may approve, and the other named failure classes.

channel token storage treated as a new leak
bots secret list treated as a leak

graphEvents.label: Keychain default exposes the secret in security argv
Conversation JSONL outside the secret-literal check

label: Phase 008's default keychain path puts the secret in the security command's argv: the risk row acknowledges that security add-generic-password -w <value> is visible in ps, rates it Med, and mitigates only by documenting it and offering --store file, while on macOS security is present so the keychain is the default. Pass the value on the child's stdin instead (security prompts when -w carries no argument), keep --store file as fallback, and add an acceptance row that samples the process table during a set and finds no value.

Phase 010's conversation JSONL is outside the literal-check list: NFR-S02 checks the human message before dispatch but REQ-001 appends it before dispatching, and nothing checks the bot reply before append. Phase 008's literal check covers a body, a question, an answer, a request prompt and a delivery message, none of which is a conversation message, so a bot that echoes a value from its environment writes it in plaintext under the state root. Require the check before append for both roles, redact a matching bot message and record the match, and add one acceptance row per role.

A linked non-approver can dispatch a run but cannot answer the item it parks, and 011 never states the rule: REQ-003 turns any linked chat message into an enqueue request, while REQ-005 refuses an answer from anyone not owner or in members. A linked team member can start work that parks a question they may not answer. Add one sentence choosing refusal before dispatch or announcement to every roster member, and one acceptance row.

direction: Treating the run record as a secret-capture path
reason: DispatchSnapshot holds source, timestamps, lateness, skipped slots and a held slot, with no environment or argv field, so the never-the-run-record claim holds by construction.

direction: Treating channel token storage as a new leak
reason: Phase 011 resolves a token through the vault at send time and refuses secret-unknown before the I/O, so the token lives in the same store as every other secret.

direction: Treating bots secret list as a leak
reason: REQ-003 prints names and metadata only and states that no verb prints a value.

direction: Treating a forwarded pairing code as a plan defect
reason: The code is one-time and the lockout is file-backed; whoever redeems it first becomes the linked actor, the same trust model as any device-pairing flow.
